- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- When the history includes recent spikes (e.g., >85), model often overshoots the true value in the immediate next period.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–20 day window; tends to hold high values longer than observed.
- Forecasting from a low-history baseline (e.g., <80) often leads to overcorrection or underestimation, especially if the true outcome is volatile.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — underestimates sharp declines until 3–5 days later.
- When true outcome shows a clear downward trend, model often holds or slightly increases forecast, missing the turn.
- Model tends to overfit recent high values, especially if the last 5–7 days are above 85, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasting from a high-history baseline (e.g., >85) often results in overestimation of the next period, then rapid correction — model doesn’t adjust smoothly.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when the history includes a recent low (e.g., <80) followed by a rebound — fails to anticipate the rebound’s magnitude.
- Model often fails to account for seasonal or event-driven volatility — especially in the 10–20 day window — leading to persistent bias.
